`ClauseRow::kind`'s doc (:3740-ish, the column the seam type carries) widens: `None` inside a `RequirementRow` is the requirement's clause, and `None` at the top level is the **root member's**. Two homes for one absence, distinguished by nesting, not by a new column.

edit.description: `Predicate::ReachedFrom { roots, via }` joins the closed enum (:132). `roots` is a requirement name — the closure's roots are its satisfiers, named exactly as `Membership`'s `target` names its source set (:318), so it rides the `target` column and no second naming scheme appears. `via` is the field set DEGREE-FIELD-SET-FILTER lands on the shared `fields` column. `key()` (:634) answers `reached-from`; `ranges_over_selection` (:664) is true beside `degree`; `target()` (:694) and `documented_field()` (:750) are `None` (it names no one field — the `mention-reachable` precedent) and `declared_keys` (:800) skips it; `predicate_from_row` (:543) decodes the `target` + `fields` columns and never the `field` one, which carries only the synthesized label segment.

The set-predicate arms the variant rides: `judge` (:611) leaves it to the graph exactly as `degree` is left (:646), and the per-member arms at :265/:320/:367/:520/:1222 list it with the other selection predicates. `admissibility` (:451) gains its two vacuity cases, both by standing precedent: an empty `roots` names no requirement to root from (`membership`'s rule verbatim), and an empty `via` follows no field — the closure would be the root set, so every non-root member fires, the false positive a directionless `degree` is already refused for.

New `reached_from` beside `degree` (:307), taking the same `(&[Selection], &[ResolvedEdge], &[ResolvedEdge])`. Opt-in through `any_clause_of` (:276), so a corpus declaring no such clause does no closure work. Per clause: the roots are the members of the `Selector::OptIn(roots)` selection — read off the same `selections` slice `engine::out_of_set` reads for `membership`, not a second satisfier walk — then a forward BFS over the via-filtered adjacency, reusing the per-clause field filter DEGREE-FIELD-SET-FILTER factors out rather than re-filtering. A visited set makes the closure well-defined over cycles; a root holds trivially by construction. One diagnostic per selected member outside the closure, at the clause's own severity, naming the roots requirement and the via set.

Wire `graph::reached_from` after the `degree` call (:563), reading the hoisted `resolved_edges` (:548) and `mention_edges` the two graph judges above it already share, plus the one `selections` list that holds both the opt-in and by-kind bindings (:497-:499) — the roots resolve off it, so no new corpus walk enters the gate.

`ClauseRow::target`'s doc (:3765) widens to two owners — `membership`'s allowed-set source and `reached-from`'s roots requirement — and `to_table` (:4737) / `from_table` (:4803) write and read it for either predicate. The via set needs no column of its own: it is the `fields` column DEGREE-FIELD-SET-FILTER adds.

The keystroke-schema skip arm (:115-:128, where `mention-reachable` and `degree` already sit): a graph-scope predicate constrains no field of a document, so it contributes nothing to an emitted JSON Schema.
Generated, never hand-edited: re-blessed with `BLESS_SEAM_BINDINGS=1 cargo test --test seam_bindings_current` after the `target` column's doc widens.

The judge's cases beside the `degree` ones: a member the roots reach transitively passes and an unlinked one fires; a root holds trivially; a cycle inside the closure terminates and changes no verdict; a via set naming one field ignores another field's arcs; a mention or import field counts only where the via set names it; and a selection with no `reached-from` clause produces no finding.
The declaration round trip: a `reached-from` row survives write→read with its `target` and `fields` columns intact, and lifts back into the same predicate.

`covered_rule`'s exhaustive `Predicate` match (:165-:188) — a new variant is a compile error until it joins the schema-silent arm, which is the correct verdict: a graph-scope predicate measures no manifest rule.

`gate_resolved_edge_walk_is_hoisted_per_gate_invocation` (:411) enumerates the hoisted walk's consumers; `reached_from` joins that list, and the opt-in claim is pinned the way `degree`'s is — no closure runs when no clause declares one.
